cite.quote: in the Normandy landings on 6 June 1944

summary.text: The landing beach from Courseulles to Saint-Aubin-sur-Mer, between the British beaches Gold and Sword. Under British Second Army, it was assaulted by the 3rd Canadian Infantry Division, with tanks of the 2nd Canadian Armoured Brigade, landing in the Mike and Nan sectors. The D-Day objectives were to cut the Caen–Bayeux road, seize Carpiquet airfield west of Caen and link the two British beaches on either flank.
